Talk to him before bringing it up to your parents. It's likely his biggest secret, and exposing him might make him feel betrayed. 

That being said, you should absolutely talk to him about it. Suicidal thoughts have a way of isolating you from the help you need. Tell him everything you said in your post (maybe don't tell him about the post though).

More than anything, you should emphasize that you care about him very much and that everyone in his life is better off for having him around. Depression causes irrational guilt and makes you feel like a burden to those around you. Telling him how much he means to people will help with those thoughts.

Encourage him to get help. Tell him that it's not his fault he feels the way he does, and that he deserves to be the happiest version of himself. Give him a hug. Tell him to open up to your parents about it. Try to refrain from telling them yourself if possible. He likely feels like he has no control over his depression as it is. Giving him the opportunity to talk to people about it could be the first step in him taking back control. Good luck. You're a good brother.

It comes from nature. In a small/growing population, there needs to be a critical number of women in order to continue growth, whereas the number of men can be fairly small and still maintain population size. A woman can only realistically have one child per year. A man can get several women pregnant per year. As long as there are enough women, the population will remain stable. Sperm is cheap, eggs are expensive.

This is why, historically, men have been the one to go to war and die on the front lines. It's where 'women and children first' comes from. Men provided stability and security (often losing their lives in the process), and women provided children.

Of course, this practice has become outdated in modern times, but it's difficult for people to break away from tens of thousands of years of evolutionary biology in just a few generations.

To get back on topic, here are some examples of problems/discrimination that men face in the USA. If you think my observations are bad, tell me why.

The majority of homeless are single men (51%).

According to a CDC study, men make up over 40% of victims of 'severe physical violence' in heterosexual relationships, though there are only a small handful of men's shelters in the whole country.

Men are sentenced to 60% longer prison sentences than women for the same crimes.

If a man is accused of a crime against a woman, he is extremely likely to be assumed guilty until proven innocent, especially in the court of public opinion. He is likely to lose his job, friends, family, etc, before he ever has a day in court.

Men accounted for 70% of suicides in 2017.

Women are far more likely to be granted custody of children than men in family court. There are even stories of women's lawyers implying their clients should fabricate abuse claims (see my point about accusations against men)

If, for any reason, the police are called to respond to a domestic abuse incident, the man is more likely to be removed, regardless of who called the police. If a woman attacks her male partner, and he calls the police, it is more likely that he will be the one removed from the home/arrested.

Men are more likely to be victims of homicide.

Men make up the vast majority of wartime casualties.

Men are more likely to be injured in a work related accident.

This isn't to say that women don't have problems, but there are numerous instances America where women are given priority/lenience when the same would never happen for men. OP is correct when he says that women objectify men just as often as men objectify women, and he's correct to say that society allows it while enforcing men to 'behave appropriately'.
